correct_completion: I will have been working here for ten years.
full_sentence: By next June, I will have been working here for ten years.
acceptable_variants: I will have worked here for a decade.
I will have spent ten years working here.

options.text: I have been working here for ten years.
options.why_wrong: The present perfect continuous looks back from now and does not fit a future point marked by 'by next June'.

options.text: I will have been working here for ten years.
I was working here for ten years.
options.why_wrong: The past continuous describes a past period, but the stem points to a future time.

options.text: I worked here for ten years.
options.why_wrong: The simple past refers to a finished period in the past and cannot complete a future time expression.

grammar_focus: Future perfect continuous with 'by' for duration up to a future point
explanation: The future perfect continuous shows an action that will still be in progress up to a future point, here marked by 'by next June'. Spanish speakers often use a simple future or a present form here, because Spanish has no direct equivalent that combines future, perfect and continuous meaning in the same way.
translation: Para junio del próximo año, habré estado trabajando aquí durante diez años.
